# Control Narrative – BR-500, Section 5: pH and Dissolved Oxygen Control

**System:** BR-500, 2000 L single-use CHO bioreactor, DeltaV DCS
**Status:** DRAFT for SME and QA review
**Convention:** Each "shall" statement has a unique ID (PH-xx, DO-xx, PM-xx, SP-xx) so OQ test cases can trace to it. Values marked **[TBC]** are proposed defaults that Process Development, Automation or QA must confirm before approval. Open items are collected in §5.10.

---

## 5.1 Scope

This section covers measurement selection, control strategy, limits, phase behaviour, alarms and setpoint-change recording for pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) on BR-500. It does not cover temperature, pressure, level, feeds or the agitator's own speed loop tuning. SIC-530 is covered here only as a DO cascade element.

## 5.2 Instruments and Final Elements

| Tag | Description | Range / Units | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| AT-501A / AT-501B | pH probes A and B | 0–14 pH [TBC: transmitter range] | pH measurement |
| FCV-510 | CO₂ sparge flow controller | 0–2 slpm | pH acid-side actuator |
| P-520 | 1 M Na₂CO₃ base pump | 0–100 % [TBC: variable speed or on/off] | pH base-side actuator |
| WT-521 | Base bag load cell | kg | Base addition totalisation |
| AT-502A / AT-502B | DO probes A and B | 0–100 % air saturation [TBC: 0–200 %?] | DO measurement |
| SIC-530 | Agitator speed controller | 80–140 rpm (DO cascade range) | DO cascade element 1 |
| FCV-511 | Air sparge flow controller | 0–10 slpm | DO cascade element 2 |
| FCV-512 | O₂ sparge flow controller | 0–5 slpm | DO cascade element 3 |

## 5.3 Phase Applicability (ISA-88)

| Phase | pH control | DO control | Base totaliser |
|---|---|---|---|
| Media Fill | Inactive | Inactive | Not running |
| Equilibrate | **Active** | **Active** | Reset and started at phase start |
| Inoculate | **Active** | **Active** | Running |
| Production | **Active** | **Active** | Running |
| Harvest | Inactive | Inactive | Frozen, value retained for batch record |

- **PH-01 / DO-01:** pH and DO control shall be inactive during Media Fill and Harvest. While inactive:
  - FCV-510, FCV-511 and FCV-512 shall be at 0 slpm.
  - P-520 shall be stopped.
  - SIC-530 shall not be driven by the DO controller. Agitator speed in these phases is defined by the phase logic in §[x].
- **PH-02 / DO-02:** At the start of Equilibrate, the pH and DO controllers shall be placed in Auto automatically. Their setpoints shall come from the recipe (defaults 7.00 pH and 40 % air saturation).
- **PH-03 / DO-03:** Control shall stay active, without re-initialising, across the Equilibrate → Inoculate → Production transitions. The transition shall be bumpless: final-element outputs shall not step at the phase change.
- **PH-04 / DO-04:** At the transition into Harvest, the controllers shall be placed in Manual and outputs driven to the inactive states in PH-01/DO-01.
- **PM-01 – Hold, Stop and Abort:**
  - When the active phase (Equilibrate to Production) goes to **Held**, pH and DO control shall continue in Auto, because the culture must be maintained.
  - On **Stopped** or **Aborted**, outputs shall go to [TBC: either the inactive states or hold last values]. This decision needs PD input, since dropping gas flow and agitation will harm the culture.
- **PM-02:** The operator shall be able to place the pH or DO controller in Manual during active phases only with the [TBC: Supervisor] role. Manual mode during Production shall raise an alarm and be recorded (see SP-06).

## 5.4 Probe Management (applies to pH and DO)

### 5.4.1 Probe health
- **PM-10:** A probe shall be declared **unhealthy** when any of the following is true:
  - DeltaV signal status is Bad (hardware, communication or sensor fault).
  - The PV is outside its valid range: pH < [TBC 6.0] or > [TBC 8.0]; DO < [TBC 0 %] or > [TBC 150 %].
  - The operator has manually removed the probe from service (Supervisor role, recorded with reason).
- **PM-11:** A probe returning from unhealthy to healthy shall not be used for control again until the operator restores it manually. There shall be no automatic re-inclusion.

### 5.4.2 Control PV selection
- **PM-12:** If both probes are healthy, the control PV shall be the arithmetic mean of A and B.
- **PM-13:** If exactly one probe is healthy, the control PV shall be that probe alone. A "single probe control" alarm shall be raised.
- **PM-14:** If neither probe is healthy, a "PV failed" alarm shall be raised and the loop shall enter its failed-PV state:
  - **pH:** P-520 stopped; FCV-510 held at its last output [TBC].
  - **DO:** cascade output held at its last value [TBC].
  - The controller shall not resume automatic action until at least one probe is restored (PM-11).

### 5.4.3 Probe disagreement
- **PM-15:** If both probes are healthy but |A − B| exceeds the deviation limit for longer than the delay time, a "probe deviation" alarm shall be raised.
  - pH: 0.10 pH for 60 s [TBC]
  - DO: 10 % air saturation for 60 s [TBC]
- **PM-16:** While the deviation alarm is active, control shall continue on the average until the operator removes one probe from service (PM-10). [TBC: QA/PD may prefer to freeze outputs instead.]

## 5.5 pH Control

### 5.5.1 Strategy
pH is controlled by a single PID controller (PHIC-501) acting on the selected PV (§5.4). Its output is split across two actuators, with a deadband between them:
- **High pH** (above setpoint) is corrected by adding CO₂ through FCV-510.
- **Low pH** (below setpoint) is corrected by adding base through P-520.

### 5.5.2 Requirements
- **PH-10:** Setpoint default is 7.00 pH. The operator-adjustable range is 6.80–7.20 pH [TBC]. Entries outside this range shall be rejected.
- **PH-11:** The deadband is ±0.05 pH around setpoint, giving 6.95–7.05 at SP 7.00. [TBC: confirm whether "0.05" means ±0.05 or a total band width of 0.05.]
- **PH-12:** While the PV is within the deadband:
  - P-520 shall be stopped.
  - FCV-510 shall hold its last output.
  - PID integral action shall be suspended.
- **PH-13:** When PV > SP + deadband:
  - FCV-510 shall be modulated by the controller between 0 and 2 slpm.
  - P-520 shall remain stopped.
- **PH-14:** When PV < SP − deadband:
  - FCV-510 shall be driven to 0 slpm.
  - P-520 shall be modulated by the controller.
  - [TBC: if P-520 is on/off, the pump shall be time-proportioned with a cycle time of [TBC] s.]
- **PH-15:** CO₂ addition and base addition shall never occur at the same time. If FCV-510 flow is above [TBC 0.02] slpm, P-520 shall not run.
- **PH-16:** FCV-510 setpoint shall be clamped to 0–2 slpm. P-520 output shall be clamped to 0–[TBC max] %.

### 5.5.3 Base addition limit (40 L per batch)
- **PH-20 – Volume calculation:** Base added shall be calculated from WT-521 as follows:
  - Base added (L) = Σ (W_ref − W_current) ÷ ρ
  - ρ is the base density, 1.10 kg/L [TBC: confirm for 1 M Na₂CO₃ at operating temperature].
  - W_ref is captured at the start of Equilibrate.
- **PH-21:** The totaliser shall be non-decreasing. An increase in WT-521 reading, such as from noise or bag handling, shall not reduce the totalised volume.
- **PH-22 – Bag change:** [TBC: bag changes are either not permitted during a batch, or follow a defined procedure.] If permitted, the procedure shall:
  - inhibit P-520,
  - accumulate the volume added so far,
  - capture a new W_ref after the change.
- **PH-23:** At 36 L (90 %) [TBC], a "base high" warning alarm shall be raised.
- **PH-24:** At 40.0 L, base addition shall be interlocked off for the rest of the batch:
  - P-520 shall stop and remain stopped.
  - A "base limit reached" alarm shall be raised.
  - The acid side (FCV-510) shall continue to operate normally.
- **PH-25:** The base limit interlock shall be reset only by starting a new batch (Media Fill). No operator override shall be possible. [TBC: QA to confirm no override path.]
- **PH-26:** If WT-521 status is Bad, P-520 shall be inhibited and an alarm raised, because the 40 L limit cannot be enforced without the load cell. Acid-side control shall continue.
- **PH-27:** The totalised base volume shall be displayed to the operator and recorded to the batch record at end of Production.

## 5.6 DO Control

### 5.6.1 Strategy
DO is controlled by a single PID controller (DOIC-502) acting on the selected PV (§5.4). Its output (0–100 %) drives three elements in sequence. Each element is used fully before the next one starts. As oxygen demand falls, the elements are released in reverse order.

| DOIC-502 output | SIC-530 agitator | FCV-511 air | FCV-512 O₂ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 % | 80 rpm | 0 slpm | 0 slpm |
| 0 → 33.3 % | 80 → 140 rpm (linear) | 0 slpm | 0 slpm |
| 33.3 → 66.7 % | 140 rpm | 0 → 10 slpm (linear) | 0 slpm |
| 66.7 → 100 % | 140 rpm | 10 slpm | 0 → 5 slpm (linear) |

[TBC: the equal one-third segment split is a proposal. Segment breakpoints may be tuned during commissioning and frozen before OQ.]

### 5.6.2 Requirements
- **DO-10:** Setpoint default is 40 % air saturation. The operator-adjustable range is 20–60 % [TBC]. Entries outside this range shall be rejected.
- **DO-11:** While DO control is active, DOIC-502 shall write a remote setpoint to SIC-530. SIC-530 shall be in Cascade mode. Agitator speed shall not go below 80 rpm while DO control is active.
- **DO-12:** FCV-511 shall not rise above 0 slpm until the SIC-530 setpoint has reached 140 rpm.
- **DO-13:** FCV-512 shall not rise above 0 slpm until the FCV-511 setpoint has reached 10 slpm.
- **DO-14:** As output decreases, the elements shall be released in reverse order:
  1. O₂ to 0 slpm first,
  2. then air to 0 slpm,
  3. then agitator to 80 rpm.
- **DO-15:** Element setpoints shall be clamped to their ranges: 80–140 rpm, 0–10 slpm and 0–5 slpm.
- **DO-16:** If SIC-530 leaves Cascade mode, or any element reports a fault, an alarm shall be raised. [TBC: decide whether the cascade then skips the faulted element or holds output.]
- **DO-17:** PID anti-windup shall prevent integral windup when all elements are at maximum (output = 100 %) or minimum (output = 0 %).

## 5.7 Setpoint Change Recording (QA requirement)

- **SP-01:** During the **Production** phase, any operator change to the pH or DO setpoint shall require a reason before the change is accepted:
  - The reason is entered as a mandatory comment, chosen from a predefined list plus free text [TBC].
  - The change is applied through DeltaV electronic signature / confirm function [TBC: single or dual signature].
- **SP-02:** If the operator cancels the reason prompt or leaves it blank, the setpoint shall be unchanged.
- **SP-03:** For each accepted change, the audit trail shall record:
  - user ID,
  - date and time,
  - tag,
  - old value and new value,
  - reason,
  - batch ID and phase.
- **SP-04:** Setpoint changes made by the recipe (for example, a recipe-defined pH shift) shall be recorded automatically with the recipe/step reference. No operator reason is required for these.
- **SP-05:** In Equilibrate and Inoculate, setpoint changes shall be recorded in the audit trail, but no reason shall be required. [TBC: QA to confirm.]
- **SP-06 (recommended):** During Production, the following changes shall also require a reason and be recorded the same way, because they affect process control as much as setpoint changes do:
  - controller mode changes (Auto/Manual),
  - manual output changes,
  - probe in/out of service actions,
  - deadband changes.
- **SP-07:** Tuning parameters, deadband, segment breakpoints, base limit and density shall be changeable only by the Engineer role. They shall not be adjustable from operator displays.

## 5.8 Alarms

| ID | Condition | Delay | Priority [TBC] | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AL-01 | pH PV deviation from SP > 0.15 [TBC] | 5 min | High | Alarm only |
| AL-02 | DO PV < 20 % or > 80 % [TBC] | 5 min | High | Alarm only |
| AL-03 | Single probe control (pH or DO) | 0 s | Medium | PM-13 |
| AL-04 | PV failed, both probes unhealthy (pH or DO) | 0 s | Critical | PM-14 |
| AL-05 | Probe deviation (pH or DO) | 60 s | Medium | PM-15 |
| AL-06 | Base addition ≥ 36 L | 0 s | Medium | PH-23 |
| AL-07 | Base addition ≥ 40 L, limit reached | 0 s | High | PH-24 interlock |
| AL-08 | WT-521 bad status | 0 s | High | PH-26 |
| AL-09 | DO cascade element fault / SIC-530 not in Cascade | 10 s | High | DO-16 |
| AL-10 | pH or DO controller in Manual during Production | 0 s | Medium | PM-02 |
| AL-11 | DO output at 100 % sustained [TBC 15 min] | 15 min | Medium | Warns cascade capacity exhausted |

Deviation alarms (AL-01, AL-02) shall be suppressed outside Equilibrate–Production.

## 5.9 OQ Test Derivation Guide

| Area | Suggested test approach | Requirement IDs |
|---|---|---|
| Phase activation | Run each phase transition; verify mode, setpoint source and output states | PH-01–04, DO-01–04, PM-01 |
| PV selection | Simulate A/B values; verify average; fail A, then B, then both | PM-10–16 |
| Deadband | Step PV across 6.94 / 6.96 / 7.04 / 7.06; verify actuator states | PH-11–15 |
| Base limit | Simulate WT-521 decrease to 36 L and 40 L equivalents; verify alarm, interlock, no override, acid side still works; simulate weight increase; fail WT-521 | PH-20–27 |
| DO cascade | Ramp DOIC-502 output 0→100→0 % in manual; verify element setpoints at 0, 16.7, 33.3, 50, 66.7, 83.3, 100 % and sequencing on the way down | DO-11–15 |
| Setpoint limits | Enter values inside, at, and outside the limits | PH-10, DO-10 |
| Audit trail | In Production, change SP with reason, cancel the prompt, submit a blank reason; repeat in Equilibrate; trigger a recipe-driven change; verify audit records | SP-01–07 |
| Alarms | Force each condition; verify delay, priority and suppression by phase | AL-01–11 |
| Hold behaviour | Hold the phase in Production; verify control continues | PM-01 |

## 5.10 Open Items for Review

1. **Deadband interpretation:** ±0.05 or total 0.05 (PH-11)?
2. **P-520 drive type:** variable speed or on/off with time-proportioning (PH-14)?
3. **Base density value:** confirm 1.10 kg/L (PH-20).
4. **Bag-change policy:** are base bag changes allowed during a batch (PH-22)?
5. **Base limit overrides:** confirm QA position that no override path exists (PH-25).
6. **Failed-PV safe states:** confirm for both loops (PM-14), and output behaviour on Stop/Abort (PM-01).
7. **Probe deviation response:** continue on average or freeze outputs (PM-16)?
8. **Limits and delays:** all probe health, deviation and alarm limits and delays (§5.4, §5.8).
9. **Setpoint ranges:** operator setpoint ranges for pH and DO (PH-10, DO-10).
10. **DO cascade:** segment breakpoints (§5.6.1) and faulted-element behaviour (DO-16).
11. **Audit trail scope:** single or dual signature; whether reasons are required outside Production; whether SP-06 is adopted.
12. **Total gas flow:** confirm whether a combined sparge limit (CO₂ + air + O₂) is needed for foaming or filter capacity on the single-use bag.
13. **DO probe range:** confirm transmitter range, since 0–100 % limits PV values above saturation.
